finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: unauthenticated q parameter is f-string interpolated into a LIKE query, allowing UNION-based reads of any table in shop.db.
finding.source: request.args.get("q") at app.py:11 (unauthenticated remote query string)
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term read from query string, no validation
term spliced into SQL text inside LIKE '%...%'
rows returned as JSON, so UNION results are returned to attacker

finding.guards_checked: None on this path: no parameter binding, escaping, allowlist, length limit, or authentication. LIKE quoting is broken by payload. Python sqlite3 rejects multi-statement execute(), so stacked writes probably blocked (not verified). shop.db not in repo, so presence of credential tables unverified. Severity High; Critical if shop.db holds credentials.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:11 reads q from request.args with no validation. app.py:12 splices it into the SQL string via f-string with no parameter binding, escaping, allowlist, or length limit. app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON. No authentication decorator or check exists on the /search route (app.py:9-13).
verdict.reason: Any anonymous client can send q to /search, which app.py:12 interpolates directly into the SQL text and app.py:13 returns to the caller, so a UNION SELECT reads any table in the sqlite database. The candidate's note that sqlite3 blocks stacked statements is correct but irrelevant, since UNION is a single statement. Severity depends on shop.db contents, which are not in the repo, but the injection itself is confirmed.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated owner lookup: /by-owner returns all products for any supplied owner string with no authorization, enabling enumeration of seller/owner names.
finding.source: request.args.get("owner") at app.py:24 (unauthenticated remote query string)
finding.sink: db.execute("SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE owner = ?", (owner,)) at app.py:25

trace.note: owner read from query string, no auth check
matching product id/name returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Query is parameterized, so no injection. No authentication or authorization, and no restriction on which owners can be queried. owner column not in repo, so its sensitivity is unverified. Severity Low; depends on whether owner identity is meant to be private.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only control is the parameterized query at app.py:25, which blocks SQL injection but not unauthorized access. No auth decorator, session check, or owner restriction exists anywhere in app.py (the only other files are .claude skill docs). An anonymous attacker reaches /by-owner directly.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: app.py:24 reads the unauthenticated `owner` query parameter, app.py:25 runs an unrestricted parameterized lookup, and app.py:26 returns id and name, so anonymous callers can probe any owner string. The claimed impact is overstated, though: the endpoint never returns owner names, only an existence oracle plus id/name, and the owner column's sensitivity is unverified, so severity should stay Low.
